body:
**Original comment by agriggio (Bitbucket: [agriggio](https://bitbucket.org/agriggio), GitHub: [agriggio](https://github.com/agriggio)).**

----------------------------------------

Ok, I have extended the dynamic profiles support to allow to implement this yourself. 

Here’s how to do it:

1. Process an image and set your desired crop. For example, for 35mm in portrait mode:

    ![](https://bitbucket.org/repo/9pArXyE/images/1767148529-Screenshot%20from%202022-11-09%2009-29-30.png)
2. save the crop in a partial profile \(by selecting only the crop tool\). Let’s say we call this “crop\_35mm\_vertical”:

    ![](https://bitbucket.org/repo/9pArXyE/images/1630197309-Screenshot%20from%202022-11-09%2009-29-56.png)
3. create a dynamic profile rule as follows:

    ![](https://bitbucket.org/repo/9pArXyE/images/2447913185-Screenshot%20from%202022-11-09%2009-29-08.png)

    the key here is to match not only on the camera name, but also on the additional metadata tags that tell us that we have a 35mm crop and that the picture is in portrait orientation. You can obviously do the same for the other crops and orientations



Now this is not exactly what was requested, but I believe it is more useful also for other applications. So that’s what you will get :-\)

HTH

‌
